en: picture taken of one individual alone

examples.en: I took a solo photo for my passport.

examples.ko: 단체 사진 말고 독사진도 한 장 찍어 주세요.
examples.en: Besides the group photo, please take a solo picture of me too.
Solo photos feel awkward, so my expression always stiffens.

examples.ko: 여행 가서 독사진을 열 장이나 건졌어요.
examples.en: I got as many as ten solo shots on the trip.
I like this solo photo the best.

examples.ko: 졸업 앨범에 들어갈 독사진 촬영이 오늘이에요.
examples.en: Today is the solo photo shoot for the graduation album.

explain: 혼자 찍은 사진을 짧게 부르는 말이에요. 반대되는 말은 '단체 사진'이나 '커플 사진'이에요. '혼자 찍은 사진'이라고 길게 말하는 것보다 일상에서 더 편하게 써요.
explain_en: It is a short word for a photo of just one person. The opposites are '단체 사진' (group photo) or '커플 사진' (couple photo). It is more convenient in daily speech than saying the longer '혼자 찍은 사진'.

examples.en: I sprang up the moment the alarm rang.

examples.ko: 소파에 누워 있던 아버지가 발딱 일어나 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: My father, who was lying on the sofa, jumped up and opened the door.
Startled, I sat bolt upright in bed.

examples.ko: 내가 이름을 부르자 아이가 발딱 일어나 달려왔어요.
examples.en: When I called his name, the child hopped up and ran over.

examples.ko: 쓰러졌던 선수가 발딱 일어나서 다시 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The player who had fallen popped back up and ran again.
I woke with a start from dozing and got off the bus.

explain: 누워 있거나 앉아 있다가 갑자기 몸을 일으키는 모습에 주로 써요. '벌떡'보다 작고 가볍게 일어나는 느낌이고, 보통 '일어나다'와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It mostly describes suddenly getting up from lying or sitting, and usually goes with '일어나다'. It feels a bit smaller and lighter than '벌떡'.

examples.en: Friends are whispering something at the back of the classroom.
In the library, you have to talk in whispers.
The child whispered into my ear.
Why are you two still whispering?
Please don't whisper in the movie theater.
I can hear all the whispering behind me.

explain: '소곤거리다'와 같은 말이고, 남이 듣지 않도록 작은 목소리로 이야기하는 모습에 써요. '속삭이다'는 귀에 대고 다정하게 말하는 느낌이 더 있어요. '소곤소곤'처럼 부사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the same as '소곤거리다' and describes talking in a small voice so others will not hear. '속삭이다' has more of a tender feel, like speaking right into someone's ear. It is also often used as the adverb '소곤소곤'.

examples.en: He was so sunk in grief that he stopped eating and drinking altogether.
For days I forgot to eat and drink and just worked.

examples.ko: 할머니는 병이 나신 뒤로 식음을 거의 못 하세요.
examples.en: Since she fell ill, Grandmother can hardly eat or drink.

examples.ko: 식음도 잊을 만큼 게임에 푹 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I was so into the game that I even forgot to eat and drink.

examples.ko: 충격이 컸는지 식음을 끊고 누워만 있어요.
examples.en: Maybe the shock was big; she has stopped eating and drinking and just lies down.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리느라 식음을 전폐하다시피 했어요.
examples.en: While waiting for the exam results, I all but stopped eating and drinking.

explain: '먹고 마시는 것'을 한 단어로 묶은 말이라 일상 대화보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 보여요. 주로 '식음을 전폐하다'처럼 걱정이나 슬픔 때문에 못 먹는 상황에 써요.

phrases.example: 아들 소식을 듣고 어머니는 식음을 전폐하셨어요.
phrases.en: Hearing the news about her son, his mother refused all food and drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬픔이나 충격 때문에 아무것도 먹고 마시지 않는다는 굳은 표현이에요. 좀 무겁고 글 같은 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed expression for not eating or drinking anything because of grief or shock. It sounds heavy and bookish.

explain_en: It bundles eating and drinking into one word, so you see it more in writing and the news than in casual talk. It is mostly used in '식음을 전폐하다' when worry or grief stops someone from eating.

examples.en: I boiled the brisket for a long time to make the broth.
Please give me a geun of brisket at the butcher shop.
Seaweed soup tastes good with brisket in it.
Brisket goes well with soups and braised dishes.
I ate boiled brisket slices dipped in mustard.
At the seolleongtang restaurant, I ordered a soup with rice that had brisket in it.

explain: 소고기 부위 이름이에요. 줄여서 그냥 '양지'라고도 많이 말하고, 주로 국이나 수육을 만들 때 써요.
explain_en: It is the name of a beef cut. People often shorten it to just '양지', and it is mainly used for soups and boiled sliced beef (수육).

examples.en: After eating greasy food, I cleanse my palate with coffee.
I'll go buy some fruit to cleanse our palates.

examples.ko: 매운 걸 먹은 뒤에 냉수로 입가심했어요.
examples.en: After eating something spicy, I rinsed my mouth with cold water.
I ordered cold sikhye to refresh my mouth.

examples.ko: 식사 후에 껌으로 입가심하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people freshen their mouth with gum after a meal.

examples.ko: 입가심하고 싶으면 물부터 한 모금 드세요.
examples.en: If you want to clear your mouth, have a sip of water first.

explain: 'N(으)로 입가심하다' 형태로 쓰고, N에는 물, 차, 과일, 시원한 음료처럼 입안을 개운하게 해 주는 것이 와요. 명사 '입가심'으로도 많이 써서 '입가심으로 과일을 먹다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as 'N(으)로 입가심하다', where N is something refreshing like water, tea, fruit or a cold drink. The noun '입가심' is also common, as in '입가심으로 과일을 먹다'.

examples.en: On my way home from work, I bought side-dish ingredients at the market.
I have nothing to make side dishes with for tonight.
Do you want to go to the mart with me to buy groceries for side dishes?
Grandmother picked some vegetables for side dishes from her garden.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 찬거리가 떨어져서 장을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: We've run out of food in the fridge, so I need to go shopping.

examples.ko: 찬거리 걱정 때문에 매일 메뉴를 고민해요.
examples.en: I worry about what to cook every day because of the side-dish ingredients.

explain: 밥과 함께 먹을 반찬을 만들 재료를 말해요. 장 본 것 전체가 아니라 반찬 재료만 가리켜요. '반찬거리'라고도 해요. 주로 집에서 요리하는 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the ingredients for side dishes to eat with rice, not to everything you bought while shopping. People also say '반찬거리'. It is mainly used when talking about cooking at home.

examples.ko: 내일 일찍 떠나려고 오늘 밤에 미리 채비해요.
examples.en: I'm getting ready ahead of time tonight to leave early tomorrow.
I hurried to get ready before the guests arrived.

examples.ko: 아이들이 학교 갈 채비하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the kids getting ready for school.

examples.ko: 비가 그치면 바로 나갈 수 있게 채비해 두세요.
examples.en: Get ready so you can head out right when the rain stops.

examples.ko: 이사하려고 채비한 지 벌써 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's already been a month since I started getting ready to move.
Time goes by quickly when you're getting ready.

explain: '채비를 하다'와 같은 뜻이에요. '이사할 채비를 하다'처럼 할 일을 앞에 넣어 말하는 형태가 더 흔하게 느껴져요. 떠나거나 시작하기 직전의 준비에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the same as '채비를 하다'. The form with the task in front, like '이사할 채비를 하다', feels more common. It suits preparation just before leaving or starting something.
